topics.label: Lecture introduction and objectives
topics.groupedBecause: These remarks introduce the lecturer and outline the learning objectives regarding cancer causation and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Cancer etiology, intrinsic mutations, and environmental epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the conceptual debate and epidemiological evidence regarding whether cancers arise from intrinsic bad luck mutations or environmental exposures.

topics.label: Oncogenic pathogens and the etiology of Burkitt lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infectious pathogens drive malignant transformation, focusing on the epidemiological and molecular link between Epstein-Barr virus, malaria, and Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical radiation and metabolically activated chemical carcinogens form bulky DNA adducts and induce genetic damage.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, host susceptibility, and multistage carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic promoter mechanisms, developmental susceptibility windows, and summarize how promotional microenvironments cooperate with initiation.

topics.label: Methodologies for determining carcinogenicity and evaluating risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the sequencing, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to identify carcinogens and evaluate their risks.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and summary
topics.groupedBecause: These remarks conclude the lecture with a final recap of key takeaways regarding environmental carcinogens and risk assessment.
